title: Scalar quasinormal and quasibound states of weakly magnetized Ernst--Schwarzschild spacetime: a confluent-Heun Wronskian approach
authors: Danilo S. Ferreira, Luis B. Castro
abstract: We study the quasinormal-mode and quasibound-state spectra of a massless scalar field in weakly magnetized Ernst--Schwarzschild spacetime. In the separated $O(B_0^2)$ regime, the Klein--Gordon equation reduces to a radial confluent-Heun equation. We construct an endpoint-selected spectral Wronskian directly from the canonical confluent-Heun recurrence and its regular-to-irregular connection limit. Quasinormal modes and quasibound states are then obtained as zeros of the same analytic spectral function on the radiative and bound sheets, respectively, providing a unified treatment of the two spectral sectors within the separated weak-field problem. The resulting QNM and QBS frequencies agree with independent weak-field Ernst and massive-Schwarzschild benchmarks available in the literature. We further show, for representative cases, that the frequencies selected by the local Heun-series termination relation examined here do not satisfy the endpoint-selected quasibound-state condition. The construction therefore provides a direct horizon-to-infinity spectral condition for both radiative and bound states within the weak-field Ernst problem.
summary: This work develops a unified mathematical framework to calculate the quasinormal and quasibound modes for scalar fields in a weakly magnetized black hole spacetime. It achieves this by transforming the governing differential equation into a confluent-Heun form and defining the spectral condition via a global Wronskian. The method provides a robust, horizon-to-infinity spectral condition that matches established theoretical benchmarks.
main_problem: To provide a unified and rigorous method for determining the quasinormal-mode (QNM) and quasibound-state (QBS) spectra for a massless scalar field in a weakly magnetized Ernst--Schwarzschild spacetime.
main_result: The spectral condition is unified by constructing an endpoint-selected spectral Wronskian, which successfully reproduces known weak-field benchmarks for both QNMs and QBSs.
method: The analysis reduces the Klein-Gordon equation to a radial confluent-Heun equation, whose spectral condition is determined by setting the global spectral Wronskian to zero.
model_or_system: The system is a massless scalar field propagating in a weakly magnetized Ernst--Schwarzschild spacetime. The analysis is restricted to the separated, weak-field approximation ($O(B_0^2)$) of the geometry.
key_observables: Quasinormal mode frequencies ($\omega$) and quasibound state frequencies, determined as the zeros of the spectral Wronskian.
important_parameters: Magnetic field strength ($B_0$), mass ($M$), angular number ($\ell$), and the frequency ($\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The results are strictly limited to the separated $O(B^2_0)$ weak-field model, and the method relies on the global spectral Wronskian condition rather than local polynomial termination.
figures_summary: Tables compare calculated QNM frequencies against established benchmarks from the literature for varying magnetic fields and masses.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the weak-field reduction to the confluent-Heun equation, derives the global spectral Wronskian from the recurrence relation, and then applies the zero-finding condition to unify the spectral determination for both radiative (QNM) and bound (QBS) states.
why_interesting: While the core physics is general relativity/field theory, the mathematical machinery—reducing a physical boundary value problem to the zeros of a specific transcendental function (the Wronskian)—is highly relevant to open quantum systems and spectral analysis in other physical contexts.
